position_statement.stance: I want to make a responsive system that visualizes time as friction, not as flow. Most motion design treats time as a smooth gradient. I want mine to feel like resistance, like the user is pushing against something material.
position_statement.what_matters_most: The system must respond to the user, not perform for them. Every transition must be earned by a user action. No autoplay, no idle animation, no "ambient" motion that runs without input.
position_statement.non_negotiables: I will not let AI suggestions soften the friction into smoothness. The aesthetic discomfort is the point. If an AI suggests easing curves that make things "feel better," I reject them on principle.
position_statement.drift_what_shifted: Started leaning toward more visible feedback cues than I originally wanted. Pulled back after Record #3.

records_of_resistance.ai_suggested: AI proposed a standard 12-column grid with smooth flex-based reflow on resize.
records_of_resistance.why_rejected: A standard grid would have killed the friction. The grid is the smoothest possible layout; it makes resistance invisible.
records_of_resistance.what_i_did_instead: Designed a deliberately staggered, off-grid layout where elements snap to position via discrete jumps, not continuous transitions. The grid is implied by where things land, never by where they move through.

records_of_resistance.ai_suggested: AI proposed smooth ease-in-out transitions on every state change, with cubic-bezier curves tuned for a polished feel.
records_of_resistance.why_rejected: Easing makes the motion read as decoration rather than response. A curve that "feels nice" hides the user's agency behind a veneer of design competence.
records_of_resistance.what_i_did_instead: Replaced all easing curves with discrete frame snaps and hard cuts. Transitions land instantly at their target state; the only "animation" is the gap between frames.

records_of_resistance.ai_suggested: AI proposed soft fade-on-hover treatments with opacity and color washes that gradually intensify as the cursor approaches.
records_of_resistance.why_rejected: Hover feedback should feel like a tap on a hard surface, not a wash. A fade implies the system is anticipating the user; I want the system to react only when contact happens.
records_of_resistance.what_i_did_instead: Implemented abrupt color and scale changes triggered on hover with no in-between frames. The element either is in its hover state or it is not; there is no continuous bridge between the two.

records_of_resistance.ai_suggested: AI proposed fluid mobile reflow using percentage widths and viewport-relative units so the layout scales continuously across breakpoints.
records_of_resistance.why_rejected: Continuous reflow softens the system's stance. The layout should commit to a position at each breakpoint, not negotiate with the viewport in real time.
records_of_resistance.what_i_did_instead: Authored a parallel layout per breakpoint with no continuous in-between. Each breakpoint is its own composition; the transition between them is a hard switch at the threshold.

records_of_resistance.ai_suggested: AI proposed adding subtle continuous motion to indicate state changes for screen-reader and low-vision users, framing it as an accessibility requirement.
records_of_resistance.why_rejected: I agreed that motion-on-state-change is necessary, but the specific suggestion (subtle, continuous) conflicted with Element 3. Accessibility cannot be the trojan horse for smoothing the system back into conventional polish.
records_of_resistance.what_i_did_instead: Added discrete, non-decorative motion paired with ARIA live-region updates so state changes are announced. All motion respects `prefers-reduced-motion`, and the discrete style is preserved across the accessible path.

ai_use_log.intervention_summary:
| Moment | AI Output | My Decision | Reasoning |
|--------|-----------|-------------|-----------|
| RoR #1 | 12-col grid | Reject | Smoothness conflicts with friction premise |
| RoR #3 | Easing curves | Reject | Same |
ai_use_log.pattern_analysis: I rejected AI suggestions most often when they optimized for conventional comfort. I kept suggestions most often around technical implementation (e.g., CSS variable scoping).

reflection.kept: Technical CSS scaffolding suggestions; saved time on plumbing.
reflection.revised: Initial color palette suggestions; too saturated, tuned down to maintain friction tone.
reflection.rejected: All easing-curve suggestions; all "feel better" UX recommendations.
reflection.learning: That my aesthetic instincts are sharper when I have a default to push against.
reflection.temptation_moments: Around accessibility tradeoffs; felt unsure, AI sounded authoritative.

disclosure.text: This work was produced through structured human-AI collaboration. The author directed all substantive decisions consistent with their Position Statement. 5 Records of Resistance document specific decisions to reject or revise AI suggestions. 12 AI interactions are logged.
